card.name: Past-tense verb after a reported event
card.fires_on: Past-tense verbs such as was, were, occurred or increased right after a subject describing a reported clinical event (toxicity, reactivation, a dose, a patient). Mostly in drug-label interaction and overdose text.

modes.label: was/were after event noun
modes.description: The verb was or were directly follows a reported event or patient, before a result such as reversible or observed.

modes.label: Past action on a dose
modes.description: A past-tense verb follows a drug or dose subject, describing what was done.
modes.example: Methadone dose was<< increased>> by a mean of 22%

card.writes: It promotes past-tense verbs like was, were, had and took, and suppresses present-tense or second-person words like your and currently.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label describes in past tense what happened to a patient or dose in a reported case.
